newsitem.title: USA: Vermont gives early nod to campaign finance reform.
newsitem.headline: Vermont gives early nod to campaign finance reform.

text.p: A campaign finance reform measure has won preliminary approval in the Vermont House of Representatives.
The bill would provide public money to candidates for statewide office beginning with governor and lieutenant governor in year 2000.
In exchange, candidates would agree to limitations on spending and fundraising.
But the House rejected amendments aimed at closing loopholes on so-called "soft money" for political parties, and alternatives to the funding source, a surcharge on state tax returns.
The votes broke down along party lines, with Democrats supporting the bill as written and Republicans opposing it.
